_comment: Held-out swap eval crossing ARGUMENT scale-type against ANSWER type.
WHY. flexible-generalization confounds the two: every numbers template has a
numeric argument AND (bar first_letter) a numeric answer, so its headline
cannot say which axis the gsm8k gain rides on. On that set the gain appeared
in every cell whose ARGUMENT lay on an ordered scale (integers, months) and
in none whose argument was an unordered category (animals, countries),
regardless of answer type -- numbers/first_letter (numeric arg, letter
answer) gained most, animals/legs (categorical arg, number-word answer)
gained nothing. Here the axes move independently.
PREDICTION, recorded before running: the gsm8k-averaged lens lifts weekdays
and ordinals on BOTH answer types, and lifts neither sports nor instruments.
TWO MATCHED CONTROLS make this more than four one-sided comparisons:
* first_letter runs in all four categories -- answer type held exactly
constant while argument scale-type varies.
* letter_count runs in weekdays (ordered) and instruments (unordered) --
the SAME orthographic operation and the same numeric answer type, so a
difference between them is attributable to the argument alone.
CONSTRAINTS ENFORCED BY tests/test_heldout.py:
* answers within a func are pairwise distinct, so a swap cannot be scored
correct by landing on another argument's answer;
* every arg and every answer is single-token in Qwen3 (checked in the
tokenizer test) -- resolve_targets silently DROPS multi-token args, and
an early draft used banjo/mandolin, which would have left instruments
with two arguments and looked like a null result;
* no ARGUMENT appears in flexible-generalization, so the eval is held out
from the data that generated the hypothesis. The first_letter TEMPLATE is
deliberately identical to the original's -- that is the point of it: the
original numbers/first_letter was gsm8k's single largest gain (0/12 to
7/12), and running the very same operation over ordered and unordered
arguments is what turns that observation into a test.
weekdays/position anchors its convention in the template, because
Sunday-first versus Monday-first would otherwise make the answer ambiguous.

Weekday arguments are capitalised because single_token_id tests exactly ' '+arg, and ' tuesday' / ' wednesday' / ' saturday' are two tokens while ' Tuesday' etc. are one. This also matches the upstream set's convention of capitalising proper nouns (France, February) and not common ones (lion, three). Getting this wrong does not fail loudly by default -- resolve_targets drops the word with a warning -- which is why run_domain_pullbacks now raises instead.
